A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTBench and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial layout changes and appendix table renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original training and certification results on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and TinyImageNet, together with analyses of neuron behavior, shared mistakes, and corruption generalization.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds three-seed accuracy summaries and a CNN5 implementation comparison in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The training algorithms, combined loss, batch-normalization fixes, initialization, and stochastic weight averaging remain unchanged. CNN5 is additional evaluation of the existing methods, rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: The reported coverage remains MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, MNIST-C, and CIFAR-10-C. CNN5 changes the model configuration. The MNIST caption in v2 Table 9 is corrected to CIFAR-10 in v3 Table 15, with the existing values retained.

E2.justification: V3 Table 14 adds a direct reference-code comparison against De Palma et al. (2024), using that implementation and its hyperparameters for IBP, SABR, and MTL-IBP. The eight-method comparison in Table 1 and the MN-BaB/OVAL comparison retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: V3 adds a CNN5 evaluation alongside the existing CNN7 experiments. Section 4.2 also changes the relative-error normalization from IBP error to the stronger model's error. The original data processing, training schedules, attack settings, and certification budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an architecture-generalization check for IBP, SABR, and MTL-IBP on CNN5. V2 Appendix A.1's qualitative assessment that PreciseBN provides little final-performance benefit is removed. Existing neuron, shared-mistake, and corruption analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 reports fixed-seed benchmark results without variability estimates. V3 Tables 9–13 introduce means and standard deviations over three random seeds for all six certified methods across five settings, plus a 3-sigma significance assessment. These supplement Table 1; Appendix A still retains its blanket fixed-seed statement.

E6.justification: Tables 9–14 add substantial result sets: seed-averaged benchmark accuracies and CNN5 comparisons, including IBP certified accuracy of 92.88% for CTBench versus 81.81% for the reference implementation. Table 1 and existing plotted values remain unchanged. Section 4.2 changes the derived MNIST relative-error figures from 7.54%/2.42% to 8.15%/2.48%.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 generalizes the formal adversarial-robustness definition and min–max constraint from L-infinity to L-p, before explicitly restricting the studied setting to L-infinity. This is a limited expansion of the formal background; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract now enumerates findings already presented in v2. The central claims about a unified fair benchmark, stronger tuned baselines, reduced advantages of recent methods, and insights into certified models retain their meaning. The conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the fragmentation advantage by matching evaluation and training radii, explicitly identifies unresolved large-radius utilization problems on CIFAR-10, and strengthens attribution of shared mistakes to training rather than verification. It also expands future directions and removes the PreciseBN convergence explanation and broader-impacts discussion.

D1.justification: V3 removes the explicit PreciseBN description specifying statistics computed from the entire training dataset at test time, while retaining the general population-statistics practice in Appendix B.3. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, timings, and code/checkpoint access information remain. The new CNN5 comparison does not specify its dataset or perturbation radius.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained, but v3 explicitly contrasts its sparsity findings with Shi et al. (2021) and connects its regularization observations to Müller et al. (2023) and De Palma et al. (2024). It also newly justifies its norm restriction by asserting the absence of deterministic certified-training algorithms for other norms.

P1.justification: V3 expands the abstract and refines explanations throughout Section 5, including aligning the shared-mistake prose with Table 2's success counts. Section 6 becomes Discussion, limitations move there from Appendix A, and Appendix C gains subsections. The main narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Six new appendix tables are added. Existing plots are reused, while appendix tables are reorganized and the verifier-comparison dataset caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: The three-seed summaries make the reliability of benchmark gains more assessable, and the CNN5 comparison adds useful validation beyond v2's fixed-seed CNN7 results. These benefits are tempered by the unreconciled fixed-seed wording, missing CNN5 dataset/radius information, and removal of explicit PreciseBN details.
